episode.title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs without exposing partial state
episode.before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, fork creation wrote the destination header directly to its final JSONL path and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, name, and labels one mutation at a time. A failure during that sequence could leave a discoverable partial fork. Torn-tail recovery similarly overwrote the original session file directly with its valid prefix, so an interrupted repair could damage the only persisted copy.
episode.after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem contract provides atomic rename-with-replacement. Fork semantics are first converted into a complete ordered mutation plan, and both fork creation and torn-tail repair build a sibling temporary file before atomically renaming it into place. Population or rename failures remove the temporary file and leave the destination absent or unchanged.
episode.diff: The change adds an atomic rename capability to the filesystem abstraction and Node implementation; introduces a shared stage-then-rename publication helper with best-effort temporary cleanup; moves fork mutation derivation into session state for reuse by memory and JSONL backends; delegates JSONL fork publication to storage so the entire header and mutation sequence is staged before visibility; and changes torn-tail truncation to publish a staged valid prefix. Failure-injection tests cover staging failure, rename failure, preservation of the original during failed repair, temporary-file cleanup, and successful reopening with fork state intact.

evidence_units.claim: Commit a838c069 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 7707 and changes ten agent implementation and test files.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0] and commit_show_stat; git show --stat a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, the repository created the final fork file immediately, then copied entries, lanes, name, and labels through separate awaited appends, allowing a failed sequence to leave a partial destination.
Before the change, detection of a malformed final JSONL line repaired the file by writing the valid prefix directly over the original path.
The filesystem contract now exposes atomic rename with destination replacement, and the Node implementation resolves both paths, invokes rename, and reports source-path failures.
Tests verify that rename removes the source, replaces existing destination content, reports a missing source path, and leaves the destination unchanged on failure.

The publication helper populates a deterministic sibling .tmp file, renames it over the destination only after population completes, and removes the temporary file on population or rename failure while preserving the original error.

Session state derives a complete, consecutively sequenced fork mutation list containing the selected entries, lane pointers, optional name, and labels; invalid branch targets are rejected before publication.

The repository prepares only the destination header and path, then delegates the fork to source storage; JSONL storage stages the header and every derived mutation before atomic publication and reloads the published file.
The in-memory backend consumes the same fork mutation derivation as the JSONL backend, keeping fork selection and metadata-copy semantics aligned across storage implementations.
Successful fork tests verify persisted message counts and verify that a reopened tree fork retains entries, lanes, name, labels, and excludes records.
Failure-injection tests verify that append failure during staging and atomic rename failure publish no fork, keep only the source session listed, and leave no .tmp file.
When replay detects a parse failure confined to the physical final line, storage stages the valid prefix through the atomic publication helper rather than overwriting the session directly.
A repair failure injected after truncating the staged file causes open to fail while the original torn session remains byte-for-byte unchanged and the temporary file is removed.

candidate_atomics.name: provide-atomic-file-replacement
candidate_atomics.title: Provide atomic destination replacement
candidate_atomics.description: Expose a filesystem operation that commits a fully prepared sibling file by atomically replacing the destination and returns structured path-aware failures.

semantic_action.intent: Make a prepared file become visible as one replacement event without exposing intermediate destination content.
semantic_action.pre_state: A complete source file and a destination path on a filesystem that supports same-filesystem atomic rename are available.
semantic_action.post_state: On success the source no longer exists and the destination contains the source content; on rename failure the existing destination remains unchanged and the error identifies the failing source when available.
semantic_action.validation: Replace an existing destination and assert the source disappears and new content is visible; inject a missing-source failure and assert the prior destination content remains.

candidate_atomics.name: derive-complete-fork-mutation-plan
candidate_atomics.title: Derive the complete fork state before persistence
candidate_atomics.description: Convert fork selection options and current session state into one ordered mutation plan shared by persistent and in-memory backends.

semantic_action.intent: Determine and validate all state required by a session fork before any destination is published.
semantic_action.pre_state: A valid source session state and fork scope, target entry, and position options are available.
semantic_action.post_state: A consecutively sequenced mutation list represents the selected entries, resulting lanes, optional session name, and labels; an invalid fork target fails before destination publication.
semantic_action.validation: Create and reopen branch and tree forks, then compare message counts, entries, lanes, name, labels, and excluded records with the selected source state.

candidate_atomics.name: publish-complete-fork-atomically
candidate_atomics.title: Publish a fork only after it is complete
candidate_atomics.description: Build the fork header and all planned mutations in a sibling temporary file, then expose the fork through one atomic replacement and clean up failed staging artifacts.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent incomplete derived sessions from becoming discoverable after interrupted or failed fork creation.
semantic_action.pre_state: A destination header, destination path, and complete validated fork mutation plan exist while the final destination is not yet published.
semantic_action.post_state: Either a complete reopenable fork is present at the destination, or no fork and no staging file is visible after a reported failure.
semantic_action.validation: Inject failures during mutation staging and final rename and assert the fork is absent from repository listing with no .tmp residue; on success reopen and verify all selected state.

candidate_atomics.name: repair-torn-tail-with-atomic-replacement
candidate_atomics.title: Repair a torn log tail without risking the original
candidate_atomics.description: Stage the valid JSONL prefix separately and replace the damaged session only after the repaired file is complete.

semantic_action.intent: Recover replayable state from an incomplete final record without destroying the original session if repair is interrupted.
semantic_action.pre_state: Replay has accepted all preceding mutations and identified a parse failure confined to the final physical line with an underlying parse cause.
semantic_action.post_state: On successful publication the session contains the valid prefix; on staging or rename failure the original bytes remain unchanged and the staging file is removed.
semantic_action.validation: Inject a failure after damaging the staged repair file, then assert open reports a storage error, the original session bytes are unchanged, and no .tmp file remains.

candidate_workflows.name: crash-safe-derived-session-publication
candidate_workflows.title: Create a derived session without exposing partial state
candidate_workflows.description: Plan the entire derived state first, stage it outside the visible destination, and publish it with one atomic filesystem operation.

workflow_graph.goal: A derived persistent session is either complete and reopenable or entirely absent after any reported staging or publication failure.
when_to_use: Creating a new persistent state artifact requires copying multiple entries, pointers, or metadata from an existing session.
The destination can be observed by repository listing or opened while multi-step construction failures are possible.
anti_goals: Do not publish the destination header before all derived mutations are staged.
Do not change which entries, lanes, name, or labels the fork operation selects.
Do not treat deletion of a partially published destination as equivalent to never publishing it.
not_applicable_when: The operation is a normal append to an already published log rather than publication of a new complete artifact.
The filesystem cannot provide same-filesystem atomic rename-with-replacement semantics.
The destination is intentionally designed to expose incremental construction.
inputs: fork scope and optional target position
workflow_graph.entry_state: The source session is loadable, the destination is not published, and fork selection has not yet been materialized as one complete persistence plan.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The destination contains a complete validated fork that reopens with the selected state, or failure leaves neither a visible destination nor a staging artifact.

steps.condition: The persistent backend publishes files through an injected filesystem abstraction.
steps.validation: Replacing an existing file is atomic at the abstraction boundary, and failed rename preserves its destination.

steps.condition: The derived artifact is a session fork selected by tree or branch options.
steps.validation: The plan has consecutive sequence numbers and reconstitutes selected entries, lane pointers, name, and labels while rejecting invalid targets.

steps.condition: A validated plan and destination header are available.
steps.validation: Injected staging and rename failures expose no fork and leave no temporary file; successful publication reopens with complete state.

validation_ladder: Verify atomic replacement semantics and path-aware failure reporting at the filesystem boundary.
Verify successful reopened forks preserve message counts, entries, lanes, name, and labels.
Inject failure during staged mutation writing and verify the fork is not listed and no temporary file remains.
Inject failure during final rename and verify the same absence and cleanup invariants.
stop_conditions: Stop if the complete derived state cannot be determined before writing the destination.
Stop if source and destination cannot reside on a filesystem supporting atomic rename.
Stop and report failure if staging or rename fails; do not expose or continue using the destination.
unresolved_or_deferred: Concurrent publications to the same destination require caller serialization because the implementation uses a deterministic sibling .tmp path.

candidate_workflows.name: failure-safe-torn-log-recovery
candidate_workflows.title: Recover a torn persistent log without overwriting the original in place
candidate_workflows.description: Identify a recoverable incomplete final record, stage the accepted prefix separately, and atomically replace the damaged log only after staging succeeds.

workflow_graph.goal: Restore a replayable log prefix while preserving the original bytes whenever repair publication fails.
when_to_use: Sequential replay succeeds through a valid prefix and only the final physical record is syntactically incomplete.
Repair requires replacing persisted content rather than merely appending a missing newline.
anti_goals: Do not truncate the original file before a complete repaired replacement is ready.
Do not silently repair malformed interior records or semantically invalid complete records.
Do not discard the original error when temporary cleanup runs.
not_applicable_when: The malformed record is not the final physical line.
The final record is complete but violates replay invariants.
The only defect is a valid final line missing its terminating newline and append-only repair is sufficient.
inputs: accepted physical lines forming the valid prefix
workflow_graph.entry_state: The original log remains present, replay has accepted its prefix, and the final physical line has a parse failure with an underlying cause.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The destination contains the valid replayable prefix, or a reported failure leaves the original damaged bytes unchanged and removes the staging file.

steps.condition: Recovery can stage a sibling file on the same filesystem as the session.
steps.validation: Atomic replacement succeeds as one rename event and rename failure leaves existing destination content unchanged.

steps.condition: The parse failure is confined to the final physical line and prior mutations have replayed successfully.
steps.validation: A failed staged repair preserves the original byte sequence and removes the .tmp file; successful repair returns storage representing the accepted prefix.

validation_ladder: Classify the corruption and reject malformed interior or complete semantically invalid mutations.
Verify the computed repair content is exactly the accepted prefix plus a terminating newline.
Inject a staging failure after modifying the temporary file and verify the original bytes remain unchanged.
Verify cleanup removes the sibling temporary file on failure.
stop_conditions: Stop without repair if corruption is not confined to the final physical line.
Stop without repair if replay of any complete preceding mutation fails.
Stop and preserve the original if staging or atomic rename fails.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle contains no CI status or reviewer discussion, so validation is grounded in committed tests rather than recorded test-run results.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle omits the PR body, reviews, comments, timeline, and status checks, so the exact reported production failure trace and executed CI results are unavailable.
The helper documentation requires serialization for publications sharing a destination because they use the same deterministic .tmp path; this commit does not add or test such serialization.
